source_tier: Third-party GitHub mirror exact AEC-named June 16 2025 generated CSV header, primary catalogue verifies named files, no authenticated AEC download or first_public_at
source_prior: McGinn & Maruyama Economic Record 2025 already documented causal effect candidates→informal in earlier periods; AEC 2025 review independently documented contemporary relation but case-selected on high informality. Our analysis confirms association, NOT novel science or replicated causal design.
restrictions: No individual/party scoring, not actually a prospective frozen evaluation, ChatRelay off, no main merge.
A: Are informal ballots more frequent with more than six nominated candidates, and does effect survive removing preexposed Riverina and Calwell?

B.Halt: Apparent difference comes only from two 13-candidate outliers

C.execution: Used prereg ballot threshold 6 vs 7+: 40 divisions <=6 and 110 >=7, mean and median informal pct. Excluded Riverina/Calwell in sensitivity (2 from long group), computed within-state contrast when both classes exist. State mixed and NT n2 opposite sign; no causal discontinuity or invented legal threshold effect.

E.negative_state_example: NT 2 divisions, difference -0.92pp, no reliable inference

F: The >6 threshold is heuristic, not abrupt change of Australian formal voting law; all candidates must be ranked correctly, and a ballot with >=7 candidates simply requires more numbering. 2026 AEC informal vote review of 25 high-informal selected divisions describes potential numbering errors, NOT representative all divisions. Limit overinterpreting causal mechanism.
G: Previous AEC review and academic paper already documented long-ballot/choice complexity, independent theoretical support but no novelty scientific attribution
J: Test out-of-state descriptive fit, not prospective accuracy.
